item.text:
**5B.6 Research Note: Productivity Foundations**
**Bottom line:** mixed, leaning positive on intent and early institution-building, but with weak direct evidence on realized delivery and continued macro/political drag in 2024.

**Positive evidence**
- **President Tinubu Establishes National Education Data System and Approves Skill Development for all Levels of Education, Teacher’s Training and Support Nationwide** | State House | 2024-04-18 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-national-education-data-system-and-approves-skill-development-for-all-levels-of-education-teachers-training-and-support-nationwide/  
  Tinubu approved a system-wide education overhaul: a national data repository, out-of-school-children work, teacher training, and skill development. This is direct evidence of investment in human capital and administrative capacity.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.4`

- **IMF Executive Board Concludes Post Financing Assessment with Nigeria** | IMF | 2024-02-09 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/02/09/pr2443-nigeria-imf-exec-board-concludes-pfa  
  The IMF said Tinubu created a fiscal/tax reform committee to raise domestic revenue for investment in infrastructure, health, and education. This supports a productivity-foundations reading because it ties reform to public-capacity spending rather than pure short-term politics.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.3`

- **Roads Infrastructure Critical To President Tinubu Devt. Agenda – VP Shettima** | State House | 2024-05-30 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/roads-infrastructure-critical-to-president-tinubu-devt-agenda-vp-shettima/  
  Shettima commissioned the 76.76km Iseyin-Fapote-Ogbomoso highway as part of Tinubu’s development agenda, explicitly linking roads to markets, schools, and hospitals. That is direct infrastructure investment evidence.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.4`

- **President Tinubu Directs Prioritization of Digital Infrastructure Investment to Enhance Business Efficiency and Productivity** | State House | 2024-03-14 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-prioritization-of-digital-infrastructure-investment-to-enhance-business-efficiency-and-productivity/  
  Tinubu ordered ministries to align regulations and tax frameworks to speed broadband and telecom investment, signaling a push for predictable regulation in a productivity-critical sector.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.4`

- **U.S.-Nigeria Reach Agreement to Harness Artificial Intelligence, Facilitate Data Flows, and Empower Digital Upskilling** | Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy | 2024-07-27 | https://fmcide.gov.ng/u-s-nigeria-reach-agreement-to-harness-artificial-intelligence-facilitate-data-flows-and-empower-digital-upskilling-issue-joint-statement/  
  Nigeria publicly committed to open, interoperable, secure internet language plus AI cooperation and workforce upskilling. This is strong evidence for technology and skills foundations, with a transparency-friendly posture.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.4`

- **Tinubu Creates PECC/EET for Economic Coordination** | State House | 2024-03-27 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-comprehensive-economic-coordination-and-planning-system-for-nigeria/  
  Tinubu set up PECC/EET around the finance minister and CBN governor, adding economists and private-sector figures, and ordered rapid implementation of the emergency plan. That is strong evidence of administrative capacity-building and technocratic coordination.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`

- **Tinubu Directs Reorganisation of the Bureau of Public Procurement** | State House | 2024-06-15 | https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-reorganisation-of-the-bureau-of-public-procurement/  
  Procurement reform is a concrete institutional move that can make state purchasing more predictable and less rent-seeking. It matters directly for infrastructure delivery and regulatory credibility.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.4`, `5B.5`

- **World Bank Approves New Financing for Nigeria to Improve Health Outcomes, Safety of Dams, and Irrigation Services** | World Bank | 2024-09-26 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/09/26/world-bank-approves-new-financing-for-nigeria-to-improve-health-outcomes-safety-of-dams-and-irrigation-services  
  The Bank approved $1.57 billion for health, basic education governance, and irrigation/hydropower resilience, explicitly targeting governance bottlenecks in service delivery. This is strong external validation of the productivity-foundations agenda.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.4`

- **Nigeria: Human Capital Public Expenditure and Institutional Review** | World Bank | 2024-06-24 | https://documents.worldbank.org/en/publication/documents-reports/documentdetail/099062424122052532  
  The report says basic education and primary health care delivery are constrained by financing and governance weaknesses. That is useful positive/diagnostic evidence because it shows the administration’s focus on structural bottlenecks in human capital.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.4`

**Negative / limiting evidence**
- **Human Rights Watch: Nigeria: 10 Years After Chibok, Schoolchildren Still at Risk** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-04-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/04/11/nigeria-10-years-after-chibok-schoolchildren-still-risk  
  HRW said authorities had failed to sustain crucial safe-learning measures, leaving children at continuing risk. This undercuts any claim that 2024 produced a materially safer education environment.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.4`

- **Hundreds Gather Across Nigerian Cities to Protest Cost-of-Living Crisis** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-01 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hundreds-gather-across-nigerian-cities-to-protest-cost-of-living-crisis-3548376  
  Reuters tied protests to subsidy removal, naira devaluation, electricity tariffs, and inflation above 34 percent. This is negative evidence on the practical environment for enterprise, households, and job creation in 2024.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.3`, `5B.4`

- **Insecurity, Rising Costs Push 31 Million Nigerians into Acute Food Shortage** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-27 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy-news/insecurity-rising-costs-push-31-million-nigerians-into-acute-food-shortage-study-says-3589474  
  The scale of acute food shortage suggests the productivity agenda had not yet translated into broad-based welfare gains. It is not a direct infrastructure finding, but it is strong negative context for human capital and labor productivity.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.3`

- **FG Spent N63.6bn on Military Equipment in Seven Months - Report** | Punch | 2024-08-17 | https://punchng.com/fg-spent-n63-6bn-on-military-equipment-in-seven-months-report/  
  Large, weakly disclosed security spending raises diversion and opportunity-cost concerns. Even if justified by security needs, it weakens the case that public resources were being concentrated on productivity-enhancing foundations.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.3`, `5B.5`

- **Nigeria Considers Tough Penalties for ‘Subversive’ Acts Under Proposed Law** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-14 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/nigeria-considers-tough-penalties-for-subversive-acts-under-proposed-law-3571782  
  A proposed counter-subversion bill was criticized as a crackdown on dissent. Even though it was later withdrawn, it points toward weaker regulatory predictability and a worse climate for scrutiny and investment confidence.  
  IDs: `5B.6`, also `5B.5`

**Search gap**
- I found strong evidence for policy announcements, financing, and administrative reforms, but much less direct evidence on realized outcomes in 2024: road quality, power reliability, hospital performance, learning gains, or job creation.
- So the best-supported reading is that Tinubu **did move to build productivity foundations**, especially in human capital, procurement, digital regulation, and administrative coordination, **but the year’s high inflation, insecurity, and weak delivery environment kept the evidence mixed rather than clearly positive**.
